page_title: Aman Check: ten minutes to check a used Mac

summary.name: Aman Check
summary.one_liner: Aman Check is a free, open source macOS app that checks a used Mac's locks, battery, SSD and hardware through guided tests and exports a dated condition report.
use_cases: Checking a used Mac before buying it
Documenting a Mac's condition before selling it
Verifying Activation Lock and Apple Account status before handover
Reading battery cycles and SSD S.M.A.R.T. health
Testing built-in keyboard, trackpad, display, speakers, camera and ports
summary.what_it_does: Aman Check runs on a Mac and reads what macOS reports about iCloud Activation Lock, Apple Account sign-in, MDM enrollment, SIP, FileVault and configuration profiles, marking items it cannot verify as needing a manual check. It reports battery charge cycles and capacity against original, plus SSD S.M.A.R.T. health, hours powered on, data written, wear and spare capacity, along with model, chip, memory, storage and installed and final supported macOS version. It offers up to twelve guided hardware tests (display, keyboard, trackpad, speakers, microphone, camera, Touch ID, ports, lid sensor, ambient light sensor, keyboard backlight) where the user records observations. It exports a dated PDF and JSON report with a QR code summary of five counts, with no overall score or grade; the page says nothing leaves the Mac and there is no telemetry.
notable: Runs read-only and sends no data over the network; no telemetry or update check
Report lists each line as measured by the app or observed by the person, with no overall grade
Sister app Aman Disk offers per-attribute S.M.A.R.T. detail and temperature history
Not notarized by Apple, so macOS requires a one-time manual allow on first launch
caveats: Not signed or notarized by Apple; macOS blocks it the first time and the user must allow it manually
Requires macOS 13 Ventura or later; older systems not supported
Some Apple Silicon readings are listed as not yet verified; developed on an Intel MacBook Pro with T2 chip
Firmware password cannot be read without administrator rights and must be checked by hand
